topicTitle: Web Utility APIs: Clipboard, Geolocation & Notifications

lessons.title: Reading/Writing System Clipboard Data (navigator.clipboard)
lessons.description: Use the Clipboard API to copy and paste text programmatically.

sections.heading: The Clipboard API
paragraphs: The modern Clipboard API lets JavaScript read from and write to the system clipboard. It works with both text and images and requires a user gesture (click) for security.
list: Must be triggered by a user action (click, keydown) for security

codeExamples.heading: Copy text to clipboard
explanation: writeText() copies a string to the system clipboard.
Clipboard operations are async — use await with try/catch.
The browser may ask the user for permission on the first read attempt.
Both operations require a user gesture — you can't run them on page load.

practice.task: Create a button that copies a specific text string to the clipboard when clicked. Show a confirmation message after copying.
hints: Use navigator.clipboard.writeText("your text") inside a click handler.
After the await, update a message element to show "Copied!".

keyTakeaways: The Clipboard API uses Promises — always use async/await with try/catch.
Write and read operations require user gestures for security.
Clipboard access may require user permission in some browsers.
The older document.execCommand("copy") is deprecated — prefer the modern API.
lessons.challenge: Build a "Copy to Clipboard" button for a code snippet that shows a brief "Copied!" animation after the copy succeeds.

lessons.title: Retrieving Device Coordinates via Geolocation API
lessons.description: Get the user's current location with the browser's Geolocation API.

sections.heading: How geolocation works
paragraphs: The Geolocation API provides the device's current position using GPS, Wi-Fi or cell tower data. The browser asks the user for permission before sharing location.
list: Requires user permission — the browser prompts automatically

codeExamples.heading: Getting current position
explanation: Always check if geolocation is supported before using it.
The success callback receives a position object with coordinates.
The error callback handles permission denied or unavailable location.
Coordinates include latitude, longitude, altitude and accuracy.

practice.task: Write a function that gets the user's current coordinates and logs them to the console. Include error handling for when permission is denied.

keyTakeaways: The Geolocation API requires user permission before sharing location.
getCurrentPosition() gets a one-time location; watchPosition() tracks continuously.
Always handle errors — users may deny permission or location may be unavailable.
Coordinates include latitude, longitude, accuracy and optional altitude.
lessons.challenge: Build a page that shows the user's coordinates and plots them on a map link using Google Maps URL format.

lessons.title: Displaying System Notifications via Notification API
lessons.description: Show desktop-style notifications from your web page to alert users.

sections.heading: The Notification API
paragraphs: Notifications let your web page send desktop-style alerts even when the tab isn't focused. They're great for new messages, updates or reminders.
list: Options: body, icon, image, tag, data
Permission must be granted before showing notifications

codeExamples.heading: Requesting permission and showing notifications
explanation: requestPermission() shows a browser prompt asking the user.
Only show notifications after permission is granted.
The notification appears as a system-level alert outside the browser window.
Always trigger from a user gesture — browsers block auto-requesting permission.

practice.task: Create a button that requests notification permission and, if granted, shows a notification with a title and body message.
hints: Use await Notification.requestPermission() inside a click handler.
Check if permission is "granted" before showing.

keyTakeaways: Notifications require explicit user permission via requestPermission().
Always trigger the permission request from a user gesture.
Notifications work even when the browser tab isn't focused.
Use options like body, icon and tag to customize appearance.
lessons.challenge: Build a reminder app where the user sets a time in minutes. When the timer expires, show a notification saying "Time's up!".
